statement: The maximum number of real lines meeting four general real lines in P³ is 2. For three pairwise-skew real input lines, the unique containing smooth split quadric Q is defined over R and the common transversals form its other real ruling. The fourth real line cuts Q in two real points or in a conjugate pair. Both cases occur on open sets of real input data.

source.location: Section 1, four-lines argument and Figure 1, printed p. 3; real quadratic-intersection consequence

scope: Four ordered real lines in P³ on the regular pairwise-skew locus; count distinct real common transversals.
notes: Elementary consequence of the cited quadric construction: a real secant fourth line gives two real points on Q and two distinct real solution lines, and the complex degree is 2. The derivation is recorded explicitly rather than attributed as a separate theorem.
